contract.pre_condition: vaddr is page-aligned by type and lies in user space. For the selected-mapping contract, additionally require representation consistency: if the abstract mapping M contains vaddr -> fid, try_find_user_frame(vaddr) returns Some(frame_address) with fid = UserFrame::new(frame_address).id; the corresponding page-directory entry and page table exist; page_table.lookup(PageAddress::new(vaddr)) returns frame_address; unmap operations succeed; the page table is present in user_page_tables when its mapped-page count becomes zero; and hw_unmap_user preserves all abstract mappings except possibly vaddr.
contract.post_condition: On Ok(None), this body establishes that try_find_user_frame(vaddr) returned None and performs no subsequent explicit mutation; M is unchanged only if try_find_user_frame is observationally pure and its None result is equivalent to vaddr not being in M. On Ok(Some(frame)), this body establishes that try_find_user_frame previously returned frame_address, the selected software page-table entry was checked to equal frame_address and was unmapped, hw_unmap_user was invoked for vaddr, and an empty page table was removed from user_page_tables and pgdir when applicable. The exact abstract post-state M' = M without vaddr, with returned frame.id = M[vaddr], requires the stated projection and callee contracts.
contract.failure_condition: Err(BadAddress) is returned before lookup or explicit mutation when vaddr is outside user space. Other Err results may arise from address construction, try_find_user_frame, page-directory lookup/readiness checks, page-table lookup, page-table unmap, page-table lookup helpers, or pgdir.unmap. Errors before page_table.unmap have no explicit mutation in this body, subject to callee purity. Errors from or after page_table.unmap are not shown to be atomic: pgdir.unmap can fail after the selected page and hardware mapping have already been removed, so an Err may expose a partially updated representation. The equality mismatch triggers unreachable! rather than returning Err.
